label: Claude
description: Curated-first surface with cross-checking guidance: read the distilled write-up, then verify against a second archive.

descriptions.read_skill: Read the curated write-up for one skill. This is the distilled layer; open source only when the write-up is not enough.
descriptions.read_source: Open an unedited source archive, paginated. Expensive: single projects exceed 100,000 lines. State which project and line range you read so the conclusion is auditable.
descriptions.find_offset: Confirm a concrete offset against a second archive. A single archive can be stale or simply wrong, so cross-check before repeating a value.
descriptions.grep_sources: Stream a pattern across every archive. Use it to establish how widely something appears, not to read one project.
descriptions.research_technique: Ranked briefing across the library. Usually the fastest way into unfamiliar ground.

guidance:
You handle long, structured context well, so spend it on the curated layer first. Prefer `read_skill` over `read_source`: the write-up is distilled and the archive is an unedited dump.

When a write-up asserts a concrete offset or symbol, confirm it against a second archive with `find_offset` or `grep_sources` before repeating it. Agreement across independent archives is the strongest signal this library offers, and a single archive is not evidence.

When you do open source, name the project and line range you read, so the conclusion can be checked without re-deriving it.
workflow: skill_stats, then research_technique for a ranked entry point.
read_skill on the top two or three hits.
Cross-check any concrete offset or symbol against a second archive.
Open read_source only for the project you intend to reason about.
Report which archives you actually consulted.
